pages.text: Reheating makes matter and antimatter in equal amounts, and they should have annihilated into light. For every billion photons there is one baryon left over. Andrei Sakharov's conditions say what it takes: baryon number violation, C and CP violation, and a moment out of equilibrium.

$(thing)Leptogenesis$() meets all three: heavy right-handed neutrinos decay a little more often into leptons than antileptons, and sphaleron transitions of the electroweak vacuum convert that excess into baryons. In a $(item)Quark-Gluon Collider$(), antimatter and sterile neutrinos in $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() leave a $(item)Baryon Asymmetry Crystal$(). With the antimatter of the Antiverse, crystals become a $(item)Baryogenesis Seed$() in the $(item)Mirror Foundry$().
